question.problem: Which value of $k$ gives precisely one solution to the equation $(1+3x)^{2}-5=k?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we solve for $x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(1+3x)^{2}-5 & =k \\ (1+3x)^{2} & =k+5 \\ \sqrt{(1+3x)^{2}} & =\sqrt{k+5} \\ |1+3x| & =\sqrt{k+5}\end{aligned}
$$

The equation has only one solution if the right-hand side is equal to zero, and the right-hand side is zero only if the expression underneath the radical is zero. So, we solve for the value of $k$ that makes the expression under the radical equal to zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{k+5} & =0 \\ k+5 & =0 \\ k & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k=-5$ will give only one solution to the equation.
